passages.text: When Israel was a child, I loved him, and out of Egypt I called My son.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about Israel.
Israel was like a child.
God loved Israel.
God called Israel out of Egypt.
God called Israel His son.
passages.original: כִּ֛י נַ֥עַר יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וָאֹהֲבֵ֑הוּ וּמִמִּצְרַ֖יִם קָרָ֥אתִי לִבְנִֽי׃

passages.text: But the more I called Israel, the farther they departed from Me. They sacrificed to the Baals and burned incense to carved images.
passages.sermon:
God called to Israel many times.
Israel moved farther away from God each time.
Israel offered sacrifices to the Baals.
Israel burned incense to carved images.
passages.original: קָרְא֖וּ לָהֶ֑ם כֵּ֚ן הָלְכ֣וּ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֔ם לַבְּעָלִ֣ים יְזַבֵּ֔חוּ וְלַפְּסִלִ֖ים יְקַטֵּרֽוּן׃

passages.text: It was I who taught Ephraim to walk, taking them in My arms, but they never realized that it was I who healed them.
passages.sermon: God taught Ephraim to walk.\r\nGod took Ephraim in His arms.\r\nEphraim did not know that God healed them.
passages.original: וְאָנֹכִ֤י תִרְגַּ֙לְתִּי֙ לְאֶפְרַ֔יִם קָחָ֖ם עַל־ זְרֽוֹעֹתָ֑יו וְלֹ֥א יָדְע֖וּ כִּ֥י רְפָאתִֽים׃

passages.text: I led them with cords of kindness, with ropes of love; I lifted the yoke from their necks and bent down to feed them.
passages.sermon:
God led Israel.
God used cords of kindness.
God used ropes of love.
God lifted the yoke from Israel’s neck.
God bent down to feed Israel.
passages.original: בְּחַבְלֵ֨י אָדָ֤ם אֶמְשְׁכֵם֙ בַּעֲבֹת֣וֹת אַהֲבָ֔ה וָאֶהְיֶ֥ה לָהֶ֛ם כִּמְרִ֥ימֵי עֹ֖ל עַ֣ל לְחֵיהֶ֑ם וְאַ֥ט אֵלָ֖יו אוֹכִֽיל׃

passages.text: Will they not return to the land of Egypt and be ruled by Assyria because they refused to repent?
passages.sermon:
God speaks about the people of Israel.
The people of Israel refuse to repent.
They will not return to the land of Egypt.
Assyria will become their king.
This happens because they refuse to turn back to God.
passages.original: לֹ֤א יָשׁוּב֙ אֶל־ אֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם וְאַשּׁ֖וּר ה֣וּא מַלְכּ֑וֹ כִּ֥י מֵאֲנ֖וּ לָשֽׁוּב׃

passages.text: A sword will flash through their cities; it will destroy the bars of their gates and consume them in their own plans.
passages.sermon: A sword will come into their cities.\r\nThe sword will destroy the bars of their gates.\r\nThe sword will consume the people because of their own plans.
passages.original: וְחָלָ֥ה חֶ֙רֶב֙ בְּעָרָ֔יו וְכִלְּתָ֥ה בַדָּ֖יו וְאָכָ֑לָה מִֽמֹּעֲצ֖וֹתֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: My people are bent on turning from Me. Though they call to the Most High, He will by no means exalt them.
passages.sermon:
God speaks about His people, Israel.
God says His people always turn away from Him.
They do not want to return to Him.
They call out to the Most High God.
God does not lift them up.
God does not honor them.
passages.original: וְעַמִּ֥י תְלוּאִ֖ים לִמְשֽׁוּבָתִ֑י וְאֶל־ עַל֙ יִקְרָאֻ֔הוּ יַ֖חַד לֹ֥א יְרוֹמֵם׃

passages.text: How could I give you up, O Ephraim? How could I surrender you, O Israel? How could I make you like Admah? How could I treat you like Zeboiim? My heart is turned within Me; My compassion is stirred!
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God addresses Ephraim and Israel.
God asks, “How could I give you up, Ephraim?”
God asks, “How could I surrender you, Israel?”
God asks, “How could I make you like Admah?”
God asks, “How could I treat you like Zeboiim?”
God’s heart turns within Him.
God’s compassion is stirred.
passages.original: אֵ֞יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ אֶפְרַ֗יִם אֲמַגֶּנְךָ֙ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אֵ֚יךְ אֶתֶּנְךָ֣ כְאַדְמָ֔ה אֲשִֽׂימְךָ֖ כִּצְבֹאיִ֑ם נֶהְפַּ֤ךְ עָלַי֙ לִבִּ֔י יַ֖חַד נִכְמְר֥וּ נִחוּמָֽי׃

passages.text: I will not execute the full fury of My anger; I will not turn back to destroy Ephraim. For I am God and not man— the Holy One among you— and I will not come in wrath.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to His people.
God says He will not carry out His full anger.
God says He will not destroy Ephraim.
God explains why.
God says, "I am God."
God says, "I am not a man."
God says, "I am the Holy One among you."
God says, "I will not come in wrath."
passages.original: לֹ֤א אֶֽעֱשֶׂה֙ חֲר֣וֹן אַפִּ֔י לֹ֥א אָשׁ֖וּב לְשַׁחֵ֣ת אֶפְרָ֑יִם כִּ֣י אֵ֤ל אָֽנֹכִי֙ וְלֹא־ אִ֔ישׁ בְּקִרְבְּךָ֣ קָד֔וֹשׁ וְלֹ֥א אָב֖וֹא בְּעִֽיר׃

passages.text: They will walk after the LORD; He will roar like a lion. When He roars, His children will come trembling from the west.
passages.sermon:
The LORD leads His people.
His people follow Him.
The LORD roars like a lion.
He roars with great power.
His children hear His roar.
His children come trembling.
They come from the west.
passages.original: אַחֲרֵ֧י יְהוָ֛ה יֵלְכ֖וּ כְּאַרְיֵ֣ה יִשְׁאָ֑ג כִּֽי־ ה֣וּא יִשְׁאַ֔ג וְיֶחֶרְד֥וּ בָנִ֖ים מִיָּֽם׃

passages.text: They will come trembling like birds from Egypt and like doves from the land of Assyria. Then I will settle them in their homes, declares the LORD.
passages.sermon:
The LORD speaks to His people.
The LORD promises to bring His people back.
God says, “They will come trembling.”
They will come from Egypt like birds.
They will come from Assyria like doves.
The LORD will settle them in their homes.
The LORD Himself declares this.
passages.original: יֶחֶרְד֤וּ כְצִפּוֹר֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וּכְיוֹנָ֖ה מֵאֶ֣רֶץ אַשּׁ֑וּר וְהוֹשַׁבְתִּ֥ים עַל־ בָּתֵּיהֶ֖ם נְאֻם־ יְהוָֽה׃ס

passages.text: Ephraim surrounds Me with lies, the house of Israel with deceit; but Judah still walks with God and is faithful to the Holy One.
passages.sermon:
Ephraim surrounds God with lies.
The house of Israel surrounds God with deceit.
Judah still walks with God.
Judah is faithful to the Holy One.
passages.original: סְבָבֻ֤נִי בְכַ֙חַשׁ֙ אֶפְרַ֔יִם וּבְמִרְמָ֖ה בֵּ֣ית יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וִֽיהוּדָ֗ה עֹ֥ד רָד֙ עִם־ אֵ֔ל וְעִם־ קְדוֹשִׁ֖ים נֶאֱמָֽן׃
